commitResults.messageTitle: Give tasks a text form for saving
commitResults.messageBody:
Add toFileFormat(), which renders a task as one tab-separated line:
type letter, done flag, description, then any date/time fields. Each
subclass supplies its own letter and fields, so a new task type only
has to implement this method. Not used by anything yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Storage to read and write the task file
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage owns data/duncan.txt: load() returns an empty list when the
file is absent, and save() creates the data folder on the first
write, so a fresh clone works with no setup. Not yet wired into the
program.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load tasks at startup and save on every change
commitResults.messageBody:
Duncan now restores the list through Storage when it starts, and
saves after each command that changes the list, so tasks survive
between runs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-7'
AGENTS.md: Adopt se-edu commit conventions
commitResults.messageBody:
The Git section asks only that a message explain its rationale, leaving
subject format and body structure unstated. The course designates the
se-education Git guide as its standard, so name the guide rather than
paraphrase part of it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse deadline/event dates as LocalDate
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and Event store their dates as Strings, so a mistyped date
is silently accepted and the chatbot can't reformat it for display.
Users need dates validated on input and shown in a friendlier form
than they were typed in.

Parse "yyyy-mm-dd" input into java.time.LocalDate in Duncan when
constructing a Deadline or Event, rejecting anything else with a
DukeException. Store the LocalDate on the task and format it as
"MMM d yyyy" in toString(). Keep toFileFormat() writing the date via
LocalDate's own ISO-8601 toString(), and have Storage.parseTask()
read it back with LocalDate.parse(), since that format round-trips
without a custom formatter.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-8'
Add test-ui skill for text UI testing
commitResults.messageBody:
Duncan's console behaviour is checked only by running the program by
hand, so a change to what it prints can go unnoticed.

Add a test-ui skill that runs every case in test/ui-test-plan.md and
compares the program's output against the expected output recorded
there. Each case states its aim, input, and expected output, and runs
in a fresh working directory so the task list one case saves cannot
affect another. Testing stops at the first failing case and reports
its expected and actual output.

Keep the cases in a Markdown plan rather than inside the runner so the
expected behaviour stays readable and reviewable on its own.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: Extract console interaction into its own class
commitResults.messageBody:
Duncan.main() mixed command dispatch logic with every System.out
print statement and the input Scanner, making the main method long
and the two responsibilities hard to see apart.

Move all console output (banner, greeting, farewell, dividers, task
list/added/marked/unmarked/deleted messages, error messages) and
input reading into a new Ui class. Duncan.main() now calls Ui methods
instead of printing directly, leaving it focused on parsing and
dispatching commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskList: Extract task list into its own class
commitResults.messageBody:
Duncan.main() manipulated the raw ArrayList<Task> directly, so every
add/remove/lookup was spread across the command-dispatch switch with
no single place owning the list's invariants.

Wrap the list in a new TaskList class exposing add, remove, get, and
size. Duncan.main() now holds a TaskList instead of an ArrayList, and
Storage/Ui still work against the plain list via TaskList.getTasks().

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Extract command-line interpretation into its own class
commitResults.messageBody:
Duncan.main() inlined every bit of string-wrangling needed to make
sense of a command: splitting off the command word, parsing dates and
task numbers, and locating the /by, /from, /to markers. That logic
had nothing to do with dispatching or executing a command, but sat
in the same switch statement as the code that did.

Move it into a new Parser class: getCommandWord/getArguments split a
line into command word and arguments, parseDate/parseTaskIndex
convert argument text into typed values, and splitDeadlineArgs/
splitEventArgs pick apart each command's own marker syntax. Duncan's
switch cases now read as "parse, then act" instead of mixing the two.

commitResults.messageTitle: Command: Replace switch dispatch with a Command hierarchy
commitResults.messageBody:
Duncan.main() held every command's execution logic inline in one
large switch statement, so adding or changing a command meant editing
that shared method, and Parser only produced loose strings/values
that the switch had to re-interpret.

Introduce an abstract Command class with one execute(TaskList, Ui,
Storage) method, and a concrete subclass per command: AddCommand
(covers todo/deadline/event, which only differ in the Task passed
in), ListCommand, MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, DeleteCommand, and
ExitCommand. Parser.parse(String) now does all of a command's input
validation up front (empty descriptions, date format, /by, /from/
/to) and returns a ready-to-run Command; the one check that needs
runtime state - whether a task number is still in range - moves to
TaskList.isValidIndex() and is checked inside the three commands that
need it, since Parser has no access to the list's current size.

Duncan becomes an instance (ui/storage/tasks fields set up in its
constructor) with a run() method matching the loop shape: read command,
parse, execute, catch DukeException, and print the divider either way.
Ui.showGoodbye() now prints only the farewell message, since the loop
supplies the surrounding dividers for every command's result the same
way it already did for showTaskAdded/showError/etc.; printDivider/
printBlankLine are renamed showLine/showBlankLine to match the show*
naming already used by the rest of Ui's methods.

One resulting behaviour change: "bye" now exits based on its command
word alone, like every other command, rather than requiring the whole
line to equal "bye" exactly (e.g. "bye now" previously fell through to
"unrecognised command"). No test case covers this edge, and it is not
otherwise expected to be user-visible.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'more-oop'
commitResults.messageBody:
Extracts Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList (Minimal goal), then
replaces the switch-based command dispatch with a Command class
hierarchy driven by Parser.parse() (Stretch goal).

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize classes into duncan/duncan.task/duncan.command packages
commitResults.messageBody:
All 17 classes lived in the default package, one flat directory with
no grouping by responsibility - fine at 7 classes, unwieldy at 17.

Move Task, Todo, Deadline, Event, and TaskList into duncan.task, and
Command and its six subclasses into duncan.command, since each group
already has a clear abstract base plus several siblings. Duncan,
DukeException, Ui, Storage, and Parser stay in the root duncan
package: each is a singular, cross-cutting concern rather than a
family of related types, so splitting them into one-class packages
(e.g. duncan.ui) would add directory indirection without organizing
anything. Went straight to this split rather than putting everything
in one duncan package first, since that intermediate step would have
had no design value of its own here - the "keep it in one package"
option only makes sense while the class count is still small, and it
already isn't.

Update the "Main class" setting in the UI test plan to duncan.Duncan,
and the one path reference in README.md, to match the new layout.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename DukeException to DuncanException
commitResults.messageBody:
The exception class kept the name "Duke" from before the bot was
renamed to Duncan, leaving the one class whose name a user might
plausibly see (in a stack trace, or if it were ever surfaced) out of
step with everything else - the class, the banner, and the greeting
all say Duncan.

Rename the class and update every throws clause, catch block, and
Javadoc reference across Parser, Duncan, Ui, and the six Command
subclasses. Purely a rename: no behaviour change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'packages'
commitResults.messageBody:
Organizes the 17 classes into duncan/duncan.task/duncan.command
packages, and renames DukeException to DuncanException to match the
project's own naming.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'add-gradle-support'
Update build.gradle fields to Duncan
Add JUnit tests targeting 50% coverage of high-value methods
commitResults.messageBody:
The codebase had no automated tests below the console level; the
text-ui-test skill confirms end-to-end behaviour, but nothing checks
individual methods in isolation.

Add 57 JUnit 5 tests covering the highest-value methods across the
codebase: Parser.parse() (every branch of command interpretation and
input validation), Storage's save/load round-trip, MarkCommand/
UnmarkCommand/DeleteCommand's bounds-checking, AddCommand, and
Deadline/Event's file and display formatting. TaskList was already
fully covered from an earlier pass. Deliberately left untested here:
Ui (pure println wrappers, already covered end-to-end by the UI test
plan), Duncan (entry point / blocking main loop), and the trivial
one-line classes (ListCommand, ExitCommand, Todo, DuncanException).

Record the 50% coverage target and the "update tests alongside code
changes" expectation in AGENTS.md, so it persists as project policy
rather than living only in this session.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for Todo, covering Task's own public methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Working toward the stretch goal of covering every non-trivial public
method: Todo had no dedicated test class yet, and it doesn't override
getStatusIcon(), getDescription(), markAsDone(), or markAsNotDone() -
so testing it through those inherited methods is also the most direct
way to exercise Task's own logic, since Task is abstract and cannot
be instantiated on its own.

Verified the tests actually catch a bug: temporarily flipped
markAsDone() to set isDone to false, confirmed 3 of the 8 tests failed
with the expected mismatch, then reverted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit test for ListCommand's isExit()
commitResults.messageBody:
execute() is a one-line delegation to ui.showTaskList() with no
branching of its own, so there's nothing meaningful to assert on
without capturing stdout to re-check hardcoded text already covered
by the UI test plan (TC04, TC05) - flagged rather than forced.

isExit() is worth its own direct test: it's Command's default, and
every non-exit command's control-flow correctness depends on it
staying false. Testing it via ListCommand rather than only indirectly
through Parser keeps this check independent of Parser's own
correctness.

Verified the test catches a bug: temporarily flipped Command's
default isExit() to return true, confirmed the test failed, reverted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit test for ExitCommand's isExit()
commitResults.messageBody:
Same shape as ListCommand: execute() is a one-line ui.showGoodbye()
call with no branching, so it's flagged rather than forced (covered
by the UI test plan's Farewell block). isExit()'s override to true is
the one piece of real logic here, and the main loop's exit condition
depends on it - worth a direct test independent of Parser, even
though ParserTest's parse_bye case already exercises it indirectly.

Verified the test catches a bug: temporarily flipped the override to
return false, confirmed both this test and ParserTest's parse_bye
case failed, reverted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'junit-tests'
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds JUnit test coverage in two passes: first targeting the highest-
value ~50% of methods (Parser, Storage, TaskList, the bounds-checking
commands, Deadline/Event formatting), then extending to every
remaining non-trivial public method (Todo/Task, ListCommand and
ExitCommand's isExit()) for the stretch goal. Ui, Duncan, and
DuncanException are deliberately left untested - flagged as console
I/O, unobservable private state, or trivial, respectively - rather
than forcing awkward tests. Also records the 50% coverage target and
its "keep tests updated alongside code changes" expectation in
AGENTS.md.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaDoc to constructors and previously undocumented methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Every class already had a class-level JavaDoc comment from earlier
refactoring passes, but roughly two thirds of non-private methods and
constructors did not - notably every constructor in the codebase, and
several of Task's and Ui's core methods.

Add JavaDoc to 31 members, prioritising the public API surface most
likely to be read by a caller: all 11 constructors, Task's behavioural
methods (getStatusIcon, getDescription, markAsDone, markAsNotDone,
toString), Todo/Deadline/Event's toFileFormat and toString overrides
(each documented with its own concrete example, since the format
differs per subtype), TaskList's add/get/size, Ui's five showTaskX
reporting methods, and Duncan's main entry point. Together with the
already-documented classes, this raises coverage from ~49% to ~91%
of non-private classes and methods (68 of 75), exceeding the minimum
target of half.

Left undocumented: execute() and isExit() overrides on the six
single-method Command subclasses (AddCommand, ListCommand,
MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, DeleteCommand, ExitCommand). Each of
those classes' one method does exactly what its class-level JavaDoc
already says, and execute() additionally inherits Command's own
documented contract via @Override, so a method-level comment there
would only restate what's already written, not add anything a reader
doesn't already have.

No behaviour change: comments only, verified with the JUnit suite,
the UI test plan, and a javadoc run.

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete JavaDoc coverage for the stretch goal
commitResults.messageBody:
The Minimal pass left two kinds of gaps: the execute()/isExit()
overrides on the six single-method Command subclasses (deliberately
skipped there as redundant with their class-level JavaDoc), and one
non-trivial private method, Parser.parseDate().

Add {@inheritDoc} to each execute() override (AddCommand, ListCommand,
MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, DeleteCommand, ExitCommand): this points
readers to Command's documented contract explicitly, rather than
leaving the method unlabelled, without duplicating a description that
already exists at the class level. ExitCommand.isExit() gets its own
one-line comment instead, since its behaviour genuinely differs from
Command's default (always true, not false) and that's worth stating
directly rather than only inheriting.

Add JavaDoc to Parser.parseDate(): a private helper, but non-trivial
(date parsing plus exception translation), and the only private
method in the codebase that still lacked one - Storage.parseTask()
and Parser's other five private helpers were already documented.

This completes the stretch goal: every non-private class and method,
plus every non-trivial private method, now has a header comment. No
behaviour change - verified with the JUnit suite, the UI test plan,
and a javadoc run.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-java-coding-standard skill, mandate it
commitResults.messageBody:
AGENTS.md had no pointer to a concrete Java style guide, so code
style relied on whatever felt consistent from file to file rather
than a stated standard.

Add a seedu-java-coding-standard skill distilling the naming,
layout, statement, and comment rules from se-education.org's
intermediate Java conventions page, and mandate it in AGENTS.md for
all Java code in this project, not just new files.

An audit against the standard found the codebase already compliant
on naming, layout, and statements; comment/JavaDoc coverage is
tracked separately on branch-A-JavaDoc and is not duplicated here.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-git-standard skill, mandate it
commitResults.messageBody:
AGENTS.md inlined the se-education Git conventions as a bulleted
list, with a note not to fetch the source page - a second, separate
copy of the same rules that could drift from the original over time.

Add a seedu-git-standard skill sourced directly from
se-education.org's Git conventions guide (commit message and branch
naming rules), and mandate it in AGENTS.md in place of the inlined
copy, so there is one source of truth instead of two.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Level 9 asks for a way to find a task by searching for a keyword in
its description, but there was no read-only way to filter the task
list - only list, which always shows everything.

Add TaskList.find(keyword), returning the tasks whose description
contains it; Ui.showMatchingTasks() to report them, numbered from 1
within the matches rather than their position in the full list; and
a new FindCommand wiring the two together, following the same
Command/Parser structure as every other command.

Matching is case-insensitive substring matching (e.g. "find BOOK"
matches "read book"), and an empty keyword is rejected the same way
an empty todo/deadline/event description already is - neither is
specified by the target, but both follow the existing conventions
most directly. Verified with 4 new UI test cases (TC14-TC17): a
multi-match search, no matches, an empty keyword, and case
insensitivity - all 17 cases pass, plus the existing JUnit suite.

Merge branch 'branch-A-CodingStandard'
Merge branch 'branch-Level-9'
Add Checkstyle configuration
Indent switch cases to satisfy Checkstyle
commitResults.messageBody:
Checkstyle's Indentation rule is configured with caseIndent 4, but the
switch blocks in Parser and Storage kept their case labels level with
the switch keyword, producing 54 violations.

Indent the case labels and their bodies one level further in.

commitResults.messageTitle: Task class: Move FIELD_SEPARATOR above instance fields
commitResults.messageBody:
Checkstyle's DeclarationOrder rule requires static variables to be
declared before instance variables, but FIELD_SEPARATOR sat after the
constructor.

commitResults.messageTitle: ParserTest: Rewrap lambdas to keep '(' at line end
commitResults.messageBody:
Checkstyle's SeparatorWrap rule requires a wrapped '(' to stay at the
end of the previous line, but five assertThrows calls began their
continuation line with the lambda's empty parameter list.

Break after the arrow instead, so only the lambda body is wrapped.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'A-Checkstyle'
Route Ui output through a buffer
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui prints straight to the console, so the only way to see what Duncan
says is to run it as a console app. A GUI needs that same text as a
string it can put into a dialog box.

Collect the messages in Ui instead of printing them, and add
Duncan#getResponse, which carries out one line of input and returns
the reply. The console app prints what it takes out of the buffer, so
what it shows is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a JavaFX GUI alongside the console app
commitResults.messageBody:
Duncan can only be used from a console, which means it can only be used
by someone willing to type commands at a terminal.

Add a JavaFX front end, following the structure of the se-education
JavaFX tutorial: a Launcher that starts the JavaFX application without
the launched class extending Application, a Main that builds the window
from FXML, a MainWindow controller that feeds each line typed to
Duncan#getResponse, and a DialogBox for one turn of the conversation.

Both front ends share the same Duncan object, so neither has any
command handling of its own. './gradlew run' now starts the GUI and the
new 'runCli' task starts the console app, so both stay runnable.

The tutorial's dependency list covers win, mac and linux; a mac-aarch64
entry is added as well, since without it JavaFX has no native library
to load on an Apple Silicon Mac.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-10'
Ui: Take message lines as varargs
commitResults.messageBody:
Each of Ui's show methods appends its message a line at a time, so a
three-line message reads as three separate calls to the same helper and
nothing in the code says the three belong together.

Take the lines as varargs instead, so one message is one call.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Varargs'
Update AGENTS.md coding standard and branch rules
Enable assertions when running the app
commitResults.messageBody:
Java ignores assert statements unless the JVM is started with -ea, so
any asserts added to the code would never be checked when the app is
run through Gradle.

Enable assertions for both the GUI (run) and the console app (runCli),
so that a broken internal assumption fails loudly during development.

commitResults.messageTitle: Assert Deadline and Event dates are non-null
commitResults.messageBody:
Both Parser and Storage build dates with LocalDate.parse, which either
returns a date or throws, so a null date can only come from a bug in
our own code. Without a check, such a bug would surface later as a
NullPointerException when the task is displayed or saved.

Assert the dates are present when the task is created, so the failure
points at the caller that passed the bad value.

commitResults.messageTitle: Assert command inputs are pre-validated
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands rely on Parser having already validated their arguments: task
indexes are never negative, and find keywords are never empty. After
adding a task, AddCommand also relies on it being last in the list,
since the task number shown to the user depends on that.

Document these assumptions with asserts. Add a Javadoc comment to the
FindCommand constructor, as checkstyle requires one now that its body
is longer than one line.

commitResults.messageTitle: Assert MainWindow has Duncan before input
commitResults.messageBody:
handleUserInput assumes setDuncan was called first, which Main does
before showing the window. Assert this, so that a wiring mistake is
reported directly rather than as a NullPointerException.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Name argument markers as constants
commitResults.messageBody:
splitEventArgs skips past the "/from " and "/to " markers using the
bare numbers 6 and 4, which are the markers' lengths.

Nothing ties those numbers to the marker strings, so a reader has to
count characters to see why they are correct, and changing a marker
would silently break the substring offsets.

Let's name the "/by ", "/from " and "/to " markers as constants and
derive the offsets from their lengths, so each marker is defined once
and the offsets stay in step with it. "/by " is included so all
argument markers are defined the same way.

commitResults.messageTitle: Command: Extract duplicated task index check
commitResults.messageBody:
MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand and DeleteCommand each begin with the same
range check on their task index, with the same error message.

Changing the rule or the message means editing all three copies, and
missing one would make the commands respond differently to the same
mistake.

Let's move the check into a helper on Command that all three call, so
the rule and its message are defined in one place.

A helper method is used rather than a new abstract parent class, as it
removes the duplication without adding to the command hierarchy.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Extract per-command argument parsing
commitResults.messageBody:
parse maps each command word to its Command. The mark, unmark and
delete cases hand their argument handling to a helper, while the
find, todo, deadline and event cases trim, split, parse dates and
validate inline.

This mix of abstraction levels buries the method's purpose: seeing
which word creates which command means reading past argument details.

Let's move each inline case body, unchanged, into its own helper, so
that parse reads as a list of command words and the commands they
create.

The check order inside each body is kept as is, so every input still
produces the same result and error message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Name empty description message as constant
Parser: Trim event description like deadline's
commitResults.messageBody:
parseDeadline trims the description that splitDeadlineArgs returns,
but splitEventArgs trims the event description itself. The two pairs
of methods do the same job, yet a reader has to check both places to
see that each description ends up trimmed.

Return the event description untrimmed and trim it in parseEvent, so
both commands handle their description the same way.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name invalid task number message as constant
commitResults.messageBody:
The "HEY! this task number is bad" message was written out three
times: twice in Parser.parseTaskIndex and once in
Command.checkTaskIndex.

Define it once as a public constant on Command and use it in all
three places. Command holds it because checkTaskIndex already owns the
rule that a task number must refer to a task in the list; Parser
already depends on Command, so no new dependency is added.

commitResults.messageTitle: Deadline, Event: Add reschedule and snooze methods
commitResults.messageBody:
The planned reschedule and snooze commands need to change the dates of
an existing deadline or event, but both classes only set their dates
in the constructor.

Add methods that set new dates directly, and methods that push the
dates back by a number of days. Done status is left unchanged, and the
save format already writes these fields, so storage needs no change.

A snooze that would move a date past the latest date LocalDate
supports throws DateTimeException and leaves the task unchanged, so the
command can report it without leaving an event half-moved.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add reschedule command for deadlines and events
commitResults.messageBody:
A deadline or event whose date changes can only be updated by deleting
it and adding it again, which loses its place in the list and its done
status.

Add "reschedule N /by DATE" for deadlines and
"reschedule N /from DATE /to DATE" for events. The reply shows the task
before and after, and a done task stays done. Rescheduling a todo, or
giving the markers of the other task type, is rejected.

The parser cannot see a task's type, so it only checks the task number
and date formats; the command checks the type and reports a missing
/by or /from and /to with the same messages used when adding. Those
messages move to Command so both places share one definition.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add snooze command for deadlines and events
commitResults.messageBody:
Pushing a task back by a few days currently means working out the new
date by hand and rescheduling it.

Add "snooze N DAYS", which moves a deadline's due date, or both of an
event's dates, later by a positive whole number of days. The reply
shows how many days and the task before and after, and a done task
stays done. Snoozing a todo is rejected with the same message as
rescheduling one.

A number of days that is not a positive whole number, or that would
move a date past the latest date LocalDate supports, is rejected with
"HEY! the number of days is bad", and the task is left unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add reschedule and snooze cases to UI test plan
Update AGENTS.md
Merge branch 'branch-B-Snooze'
Update AGENTS.md
Reject malformed command input
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands with leading spaces or tab separators are not recognised,
repeated markers get a misleading date-format error, an event typed
with /to before /from crashes the app, and events can end before they
start. Extra text after list/bye and signed numbers are silently
accepted.

Tighten the parser so each of these is rejected with a message that
names the actual problem:

* Treat tabs as spaces and ignore surrounding whitespace
* Reject extra text after commands that take no arguments
* Reject /by, /from or /to given more than once, or used as a word
  in a deadline or event description
* Require /from before /to, and an event end on or after its start
* Accept task numbers and snooze days as plain digits only

Markers are matched as whole words, so descriptions like
"fix /toolbox" stay valid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject duplicate tasks and redundant marks
commitResults.messageBody:
The same task can be added any number of times, and marking a task
that is already done (or unmarking one that is not) reports success
as if something changed.

Reject a todo, deadline or event when the list already holds a task
of the same type with the same description and dates. Descriptions
are compared ignoring case and extra whitespace, and done status is
ignored, so trivially different retypings still count as the same
task.

Make mark and unmark say the task is already in that state and
leave it unchanged, instead of rewriting the save file for nothing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle corrupt and unwritable save files
commitResults.messageBody:
A malformed line in the save file crashes the app at startup, while
unknown types, odd done flags and extra fields are silently misread.
A file that is unreadable or not valid UTF-8 loads as empty and is
then overwritten by the next save, losing every task in it. Save
failures print to the console only, so GUI users never see them,
and the command still reports success.

Load the file strictly as UTF-8, skip lines that are not a valid
task, and list their line numbers in a warning. After any load
problem, copy the original file to a .bak next to it before anything
can overwrite it; if that copy fails, turn saving off for the session
rather than risk destroying the only copy. A missing file is a normal
first run and is not treated as a problem.

Make save report failures to the command, which keeps the change in
memory and warns that it was NOT saved on every change until saving
works again. Route all load and save warnings through Ui so both the
console and the GUI show them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the app responsive on unexpected errors
commitResults.messageBody:
When console input ends without bye (e.g. Ctrl-D or piped input),
the app dies with a stack trace. Any unexpected runtime exception
while handling a command also escapes getResponse, crashing the
console app and leaving the GUI with no reply.

End the console loop quietly when input runs out, and turn any
unexpected runtime exception in getResponse into an error message,
as a safety net so no input can crash the app.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-MoreErrorHandling'
Record severity of each line of output
commitResults.messageBody:
The GUI cannot tell an error or a save warning from an ordinary reply,
because Ui collects everything into one string. A GUI that wants to
highlight problems would have to guess from the wording of messages,
and some warnings carry no fixed prefix.

Keep the collected output as lines that each carry a severity (normal,
warning or error), and derive a reply's overall severity from its most
severe line. Add showWarning for problems that do not stop a command,
such as a change that could not be saved, and use it for save and load
warnings. Expose the lines and the console banner through Duncan so a
GUI can use them.

flushOutput and getResponse still return exactly the same text, so the
console app and its output are unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add parser to split task lines for colouring
commitResults.messageBody:
The GUI wants to colour the type, status and dates of a task line
differently, but Task.toString() gives one plain string, and the console
output must not change.

Add TaskLineParser, which recognises the shape of a task line and splits
it into labelled pieces. It shows the type as a bare letter and the
status as a check mark or circle, each padded to the three columns the
brackets used, so descriptions stay aligned. Dates are set off only for
deadlines and events, so a todo whose description looks like a date is
left alone. Any other line comes back as one plain piece.

The parser has no JavaFX dependency. Its tests feed it the real
toString() of every task type, done and not done, so changing a task's
display format fails a test instead of quietly dropping the colouring.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bundle JetBrains Mono font for the GUI
commitResults.messageBody:
Task lists only line up in a fixed-width font, and the platform's
default monospace font differs between systems and may lack the check
mark and circle glyphs the GUI uses for task status.

Add the JetBrains Mono regular font and its licence to the resources,
so it ships inside the JAR and looks the same everywhere. Both glyphs
were checked against this file and have the same width as every other
character. Credit the font, its source and the SIL Open Font License in
the README, as the licence requires.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restyle GUI with a dark, resizable layout
commitResults.messageBody:
Both sides of the conversation looked the same apart from alignment,
errors looked like ordinary replies, large gaps wasted space, and the
window was fixed at one size with no styling at all.

Give the user and Duncan different shapes: the user's words sit in a
compact bubble on the right, while Duncan's replies are full-width
panels. Errors get a tinted block with a red edge, and warnings an amber
edge with only the warning lines coloured. Task types, status and dates
are tinted, and the ASCII logo opens the conversation, dimmed, and is
never wrapped. One accent colour is used for everything interactive.
All styling lives in a style sheet.

Replace the fixed 400x600 absolute layout with one that reflows, with a
minimum size set by the width the logo needs. Load the bundled font from
the classpath before the style sheet is applied, and log loudly if that
fails. Scroll to the newest message with a listener rather than a
binding, so the user can still scroll up. Add a window icon.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-BetterGui'
Rewrite user guide for Duncan
commitResults.messageBody:
The docs README was still the unfilled course template, so a new
user had no way to learn how to run Duncan or what it can do.

Replace it with a guide that names the chatbot up front, shows the
screenshot, and explains how to start it from the JAR. Add one
section per command (todo, deadline, event, list, find, mark,
unmark, delete, reschedule, snooze, bye) with its format, examples
and rules, a section on saving and recovering the data file, and a
command summary table. The Credits section is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-UserGuide'
Show original task numbers in find results
commitResults.messageBody:
Find numbered its results from 1, so a result's number differed
from the number that mark, delete and the other commands expect.
Using a result's number directly acted on the wrong task.

Key each match by its position in the full list and print that
number instead, leaving the rest of the result text unchanged.
TaskList.find now returns matches with their indexes to support this.

Update the tests, the UI test plan case for find, and the user
guide to match.
